column1: # Legacy layout paths -- deliberately NOT SSSOM.
# The SSSOM crosswalk records what a CDIF concept corresponds to in the
# NeXus standard. This table records where writers that predate or
# diverge from that standard actually put the value. Those are different
# kinds of claim, and mixing them would make the crosswalk unpublishable
# Consulted only after the crosswalk, and only for concepts still
# missing. A legacy path never overrides a standards-based value.
#   concept      CDIF concept CURIE; must exist in the crosswalk.
#   convention   Which writer produces this layout. Provenance, not
#                dispatch -- the paths name non-standard classes and so
#   path         Entry-relative, same NXDL syntax as the crosswalk:
#                name:NXclass segments, uppercase names are placeholders.
#   confidence   Lower than a standards mapping unless the legacy field
#   comment      Why this is not the standard location.

column5: NXscan and NXxrayedge are not NeXus base classes; restructured NXxas uses element:NXelement/name
written as a string with no units attribute; eV by convention at this beamline but not asserted in the file
the standard puts the beamline name on NXinstrument; this writer puts it on NXsource alongside ~20 other beamline_* fields
fires only where NXsource/name is absent; where both exist, facility_name is the cleaner value -- see comment in map/legacy.py
insertion-device description rather than a source type term
restructured NXxas carries this as ENTRY/intensity, disambiguated by the declared mode; here the field name carries the mode
free text (Transmission, Fluorescence), not the NXxas_* definition name; needs normalising before use as a mode term
crystal material rather than a monochromator type; the standard NXcrystal/type is absent
the definition puts the image at NXdetector/data; this writer stores a stack of frames in NXdata and leaves the detector group without data
beam-through-nothing image held beside the frames; the definition has no place for it
detector column coordinate; NXsas names no axes at all, since position is meant to be reconstructed from the geometry scalars
this writer splits the definition's single size into size_x and size_y; taking x alone is a simplification
